Only folders under the roots this installation allows can be opened. Until each moves to a screen of its own, the round trip of the connection and your approved devices are below.
welcomeHelp.states: Recent folders come first, pinned ones on top. A folder marked as unavailable left the allowlist or the disk: it stays listed so you know why, and it cannot be opened. With no recent folder yet the list says so, and the roots below are where to start. The roots are the allowlist — the only folders this installation lets Claude work in. To allow another, run the command shown under them on the machine the backend runs on: the web never changes the allowlist.
welcomeHelp.notRecorded: Opening a folder records it among your recent folders and your tabs, on the server, so they follow you to another device. Nothing inside a folder is read to list it here, and the roots cannot be changed from this screen: that takes the pnpm allowlist command on the machine.

Closing a tab never ends its Claude sessions — they keep running on the machine, and come back when you open the folder again. A tab whose folder left the allowlist, or the disk, opens as an error, and the other tabs carry on. A place still empty says what will live there.
help.notRecorded: Which folders are open, and their order, are kept on the server, so they follow you to another device. The layout of each tab — its sizes, the open panels — is kept only in this browser. What you say to Claude and what it answers is the session's, not the tab's; decisions on permissions go to the audit trail.

help.what: Where to look when something seems stuck. The connection shows whether this browser is talking to the backend right now; the round trip sends one command through every layer — the gateway, the rules, the database — and shows the answer and how long it took.
help.states: Connected means everything on screen is live. Reconnecting means the connection dropped and the app is trying again on its own, waiting a little longer each time: “Reconnect” tries now. When the server asked the app to slow down, the button waits as long as the server asked, and says so. A ping waiting for its answer shows as loading; a ping sent while the connection is down says so, with the way to reconnect.
help.notRecorded: Nothing here reads your conversations or files. A round trip is counted on the server, and nothing else is kept. The logs of the backend and of the app are not shown here yet.

connection.heldBack: The server asked this app to slow down. It reconnects on its own as soon as the server allows.

Appearance changes at once and is kept on this device only, so your phone can look different from your desktop. The folders this installation allows are read only here: adding one takes a command on the machine the backend runs on, which the section shows ready to copy.

screen.title: Explorer
screen.purpose: The files and folders of the folder this tab has open — open, create, rename, move, copy and delete them.

help.what: The tree shows the folder this tab has open, one level at a time: a folder is read when you open it. Click a file to preview it in the editor, double-click or press Enter to keep it open. Everything you do here — create, rename, move, copy, delete — is done on the disk of this machine, in this folder only, and is written to the audit trail before it happens. An entry with the arrow-out-of-a-box icon is a link that leads outside this folder: it is shown so you know it is there, and it never opens. An entry with a question mark has a name that is not valid text: it is shown, and nothing can be done to it from here.
help.states: While a folder is read, its rows show it loading. A folder that could not be read says why, and Enter on it tries again. A folder with more entries than the tree lists says so: filter by name to find the rest. Changes on disk — Claude writing, you in another program — appear by themselves; when this machine cannot follow the folder, a warning says so and a button reads it again by hand. Ctrl+Z, with the focus in the tree, undoes the last rename, move, new file or folder, or copy of this tab, as long as nothing changed it since — if Claude wrote to the file after, the undo is refused and says why. Undo lasts only while this page is open.
help.notRecorded: Hidden entries (.git, .svn, .hg, .DS_Store, Thumbs.db) are left out unless you show them; folders like node_modules, dist, build, .venv and target are shown but not followed, so a change inside them appears when you open or reload them. Deleting keeps what it takes in the local history first and does not ask: a notification says what went, with Undo. What the history cannot keep — too large, too many entries, or the history unavailable — is deleted only for good, after asking, with how much goes and why there is no undo. What you read is not written to the audit trail; what you change is, with the path and never the contents.
help.transfer: Drag files or folders from your desktop onto a folder of the tree to upload them there — a folder keeps its structure. Without a mouse, use Upload files here… or Upload folder here… (Alt+U, Alt+Shift+U). Files already there are shown before anything is sent: replace, keep both or skip each one. Download (Alt+Shift+D) saves a file, or a folder or everything selected as one zip.
help.transferLimits: Limits of this machine: each file uploaded up to {{uploadFile}}, at most {{uploadEntries}} files and {{uploadTotal}} in one upload; a download up to {{download}}, and a zip of at most {{archiveEntries}} entries.
help.transferUnknown: The limits of this machine could not be read right now; the server still checks them.
help.transferAbove: Above a limit, nothing moves: the upload or the download is refused before it starts, saying the limit — it is never cut half-way. Downloads are recorded in the audit trail, with the path and never the contents.

screen.title: Editor
screen.purpose: The files of this folder, open in tabs, beside the chat with Claude.

help.what: The editor shows the files of this folder in tabs. A single click in the Explorer opens a file as a preview — its tab in italics, replaced by the next preview until you edit it or double-click it. A tab with unsaved changes shows a dot where its close button was. Open a file to the side to see two (or three) groups at once; the same file in two groups is one buffer, edited in both. Ctrl+S saves the active file, Ctrl+K S saves every one, and Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the last tab closed. Find and replace (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+H) and go to line (Ctrl+G) are the editor's own.
help.states: A save names the version of the file you opened. If the disk changed since — Claude, probably, wrote to it — the save is refused and you choose: compare the two, overwrite on purpose, or reload and drop your changes; nothing is overwritten on its own. When a file changes on disk under a clean tab, the tab reloads and keeps your place; under a tab with unsaved changes, a warning says who changed it and offers the same three choices. A file deleted on disk is marked, and saving it offers to recreate it. Large files open in light mode — no minimap, no folding, no highlighting — binary files open in a hexadecimal view and files above the editing limit in a paged reading, both read-only; a file this machine does not let the server read opens a page that says why instead of the editor.
help.notRecorded: Unsaved changes live only in this page: they are never kept in the browser, so reloading or closing the page asks first. Your saves are recorded in the audit trail, without their content; opening and reading a file is not recorded. Previews, the hexadecimal view and the paged reading only read the file: they are not recorded either.
help.previewsHeading: Previews, binary files and large files
help.previews: Open preview (Ctrl+Shift+V), or open it to the side (Ctrl+K V), to see a file rendered: markdown, images, SVG and PDF; the eye button of the tab switches between the file and its preview. The preview of a markdown file follows what you type, before you save. Images and PDFs open as their preview. A link to a file of this folder opens it in the editor; images on the internet are not loaded — they become links.
help.previewsHtml: HTML is never run in a preview — not in markdown, not an .html file, not a script inside an SVG. A page shown here would run with your session, inside this app; so markdown keeps its text and drops its tags, an .html file is shown as its source, and an SVG is drawn as a picture, which runs nothing.
help.paged: A binary file opens in a hexadecimal view, and a text above the editing limit opens as pages of text; both are read-only and read a page at a time. If the file changes on disk while you read it, the view says so and starts over on the new version — it never mixes pages of two versions.
help.pdfReader: A PDF opens in the reader of this app, never the browser's own: every page in one scroll, fitted to the width. Type a page number and press Enter to go to it; zoom with the buttons, the list or Ctrl+= and Ctrl+- (Ctrl+0 fits the width again, and Ctrl with the mouse wheel zooms too); select and copy its text. The side panel shows the outline of the PDF, when it has one, and the thumbnails of its pages; Ctrl+F, with the focus in the reader, finds text in it. Links to other places of the PDF move to them; links to the web open in a new tab, and any other kind is not followed. A PDF with a password asks for it, and the password stays in this page only. Nothing a PDF carries runs: no scripts, and its form fields are not filled in. The page, the zoom and the panel of each tab are kept while the page is open.
help.diagrams: Tables wider than the preview scroll in their own box. A fenced block of code named mermaid is drawn as a diagram — here, in Claude's answers and in the plans to approve — once its closing fence is there; Show the code switches to its source, and an error says on which line it is. A diagram is drawn safely: nothing in it runs, its links follow the rules of every link here, and it never loads anything from the internet.

screen.title: Timeline
screen.purpose: The versions of the active file this machine kept before you overwrote or deleted them — compare them, and bring one back.

help.what: The Timeline is this machine's local history of the files you change from here. Before a save, a delete, a restore or an upload would lose a version of a file, that version is kept — on this machine, outside the folder. Compare a version with the file as it is now, or pick one and compare it with another; restore one to put it back. "Recently deleted" lists what was deleted from this folder and no longer exists, and brings it back where it was. Deleting what the history can keep does not ask first: a notification says what went, with Undo.
help.states: Each version says why it was kept, who wrote it — you, or another person who can reach this folder — and when, newest first; filter by reason to see only some. A file larger than the history keeps is listed without its content: it says so, and cannot be compared or restored. A file with no version yet has no history: it starts with the first save, delete or upload that would lose something. Restoring asks first only when the file has unsaved changes, which it discards; the version it replaces is kept first. If the file changed since you opened it — Claude may have written to it — the restore is refused and says so.
help.notRecorded: This is not git, and it is not Claude's undo. Nothing here is a commit or a branch, and what Claude writes is not kept here: Claude's changes are undone from its session. The history follows a path, not a renamed file. A version's content never goes to the audit trail; only that a file was restored does.
help.limitsHeading: What it keeps, and for how long
help.limits: A version is kept only for a file up to {{size}}. The history keeps a limited number of versions, for a limited time and in a limited space, as this installation sets them — by default 50 versions of each file, 512 MB in all, for 30 days — and the oldest go first.

help.states: Each group loads, fails and empties on its own: when the history cannot be read, what runs here is still listed. The lists refresh every few seconds while the view is on screen, and at once when a session of yours begins or ends.
help.notRecorded: Reading a conversation changes nothing, and nothing is deleted from here: the history is Claude's own, shared with the editor.
help.groups: Pressing a running session shows it in the panel beside the editor. Pressing a conversation opens it in the panel to read, with the button that continues it.
help.origin: "Opened here" means this app opened it for you — it says so because it keeps a record of every conversation it opens. Everything else began in the editor or a terminal of this machine; nothing tells which one.
help.forkHeading: Why continuing one begun elsewhere makes a new id
help.fork: A conversation begun elsewhere is continued as a copy, under a new id, so this app never writes into a file the editor may be writing. The editor will not see the answers given here.
help.elsewhere: Nothing tells this app that an editor has a conversation open. What it knows is when the conversation was last written: written within the last two minutes, it is listed as active. A long tool can leave it unwritten for minutes while it is still running.
help.limit: Each session is a process of Claude on this machine, and the machine holds only so many. The ceiling is the installation's: when it is reached, end a session of yours or wait for one to finish.

help.open: Help about the panel of Claude
help.what: Each tab of the panel is a conversation of this folder: a draft that becomes a session with its first prompt, a session that is running, or a conversation of the history you are reading. Closing a tab never ends its session — it goes on in the backend, and the Sessions view lists it.
help.states: While it loads, a placeholder holds its place; what fails says why, with the way to try again; an empty conversation teaches how to start one.
help.notRecorded: The audit trail keeps every tool Claude ran and its exact input. It never keeps what a file says nor the messages of the conversation — those stay in Claude's own store, on this machine.
help.modes: Default asks you before every tool that needs your word. Accept edits stops asking before Claude edits or writes a file — and the preview of the change on the card is gone with it. Plan has Claude plan without changing anything, and asks you to approve the plan. Skipping every question is never offered.
help.queue: A prompt sent while Claude works waits above the prompt box, in the order it arrived from any of your devices, and runs as a turn of its own when the turn ends. Until then, any device can take it out.
help.resend: Editing a prompt sends it again in a new conversation that continues from before it; the original stays as it was in the history. The files do not go back on their own: tick the undo of that turn to put them back too.
help.review: Accept only marks a file as reviewed in this tab — nothing is written. Reject puts a file, or one change in it, back the way it was before the session, and offers to undo that. A file you changed after Claude is never overwritten: rejecting it keeps it as it is.
help.context: The meter shows how full the conversation's context window is, by category. Near the limit, compacting summarises the conversation so far — the command of the installation, sent as a prompt — and the conversation marks where it happened.
help.notices: A question asked in a folder tab that is not on screen, or with the panel closed, shows as a badge on the tab and on the activity bar, and as a notice with the way to it. With the browser's notifications turned on, a hidden page is told too — the folder and what happened, never the command.
help.composer: Enter sends and Shift+Enter breaks the line; while an input method is composing a character, Enter does neither. With nothing written and no context, the send button stays off and says why. While Claude works, what you send waits in the queue.
help.mention: Type @ to choose a file or a folder of this folder: the open files and the recent ones come first, then what the folder holds, level by level — type a / to go into a folder. @selection adds what is selected in the editor. Use the arrows to move, Enter or Tab to choose, and Esc to close the list without losing what you typed.
help.commands: Type / at the start of the box for the commands and skills of this installation, even before the session exists. Choosing one writes it with a space after it, and says what it takes. If the list cannot be read, anything you type still goes as the prompt.
help.drag: Drag files and folders from the explorer, or a tab of the editor, onto the box or the conversation: each becomes a chip, and a folder is one chip, never everything in it. Without dragging, use “Add to Claude's context” in the menu of the explorer, of a tab, or of a selection in the editor. Items from another folder tab are left out: the context is this folder's.
help.contextSetHeading: The context of the next prompt
help.contextSet: The chips above the box are what goes with the next prompt; each one can be removed with its button. The line under them adds up their size and estimates the tokens at about four bytes each — an estimate, not a count. Past a share of what is left of the context window it warns and still sends; past the limit of a prompt it does not send, and says why. The set is this conversation's, and stays until you send it.
help.reads: A file, a folder or a range of lines goes as a reference, never as its contents: Claude reads it with the Read tool, which the audit trail records like any other tool. It reads what is saved on disk, not what is unsaved in the editor — the chip warns you. An @path you type by hand is not read by the CLI on its own: only Claude's Read reads it.
help.desktop: An image or a text file dragged from your computer goes with the prompt as an attachment: it is kept in memory for this session only, never written into the folder nor into the trail, and is gone when the session ends. To put it in the folder, upload it in the explorer instead.
help.skillsHeading: Where the commands and skills come from
help.skills: Each entry of / says its origin: Claude Code is the command of the installation itself; Project comes from the .claude folder of this project; User and System are the skills of your user and of the system. Two with the same name are both listed, and the one / runs is Claude Code's — the other says it is covered.
help.bar: What holds for the next prompt is under the box, in this order: + adds a file or a folder, a file of your computer or the selection of the editor; / lists the commands and skills; then the mode, the model and the effort, the share of the context window used — with Compact inside it — and send. While Claude works, send puts what you wrote in the queue, and Stop beside it ends the turn; with the box empty, the button itself is Stop. The effort is chosen in a new conversation only. In a narrow panel, the model and the effort move into the … of the bar.
help.menu: The … of the header holds what is done to the whole session, and seldom: end it — only the browser that opened it may, and it asks first —, export it as Markdown, undo its file changes, copy its id; and the notifications of the browser, the permission rules and this help. The dot beside it says how the session stands, with its id and what it has cost since it opened; the clock beside the + opens the conversations of this folder.
help.working: While a turn runs, its last line moves: an asterisk, what Claude is doing — the tool it runs, or a word for the turn — and for how long. Its thinking is a line of its own, in order: "Thinking…" while it arrives, "Thought for n s" once it is over, folded — press it to read it. When the turn ends, the line gives way to what the turn cost.
help.inline: When Claude asks before running a tool, the question is in the conversation, in the place of that tool: the exact command, how risky it is, the time left and how far a yes reaches. Once answered, the tool line says how — by you, on a phone and by whom, by one of your rules, or refused because nobody answered in time. A question never takes the focus from the box while you write: Enter still sends your prompt.
help.pill: With a question out of view — the conversation scrolled up, or the changes on screen — a pill above the box says Claude is waiting, and how many questions. Pressing it, or the command Go to the question waiting for you, takes you to the oldest.
help.actions: Pointing at a prompt of yours, or moving the focus into it, shows what can be done from it: edit and send it again, fork from before it, and put the files back to before its turn — with the reach shown file by file first. While Claude works the undo waits for the turn to end; once the session has ended there is no undo, so the button is not there.

screen.title: Claude
screen.purpose: Talk to Claude about this folder: start conversations, follow and approve what it does, and review what it changed.

set.label: Context of the next prompt
set.folders: Folders count as items: Claude decides what to read in them.
set.warn: That is a large share of what is left of the context window — it still sends.
set.overItems: A prompt carries at most 20 items of context. Remove some to send.
set.overBytes: The files of the context add up to more than this prompt may carry. Remove some to send.
set.overflow: Items left out, past the limit of a prompt: {{count}}.

chip.binary: not text — Claude will not read it
chip.dirty: unsaved — Claude reads what is saved

drop.here: Drop to add to the context of the next prompt
drop.tooLarge: {{name}} is larger than {{limit}} MB, the limit of an attachment.
drop.unsupported: {{name}} cannot go with a prompt: images must be PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP, and files must be text.
drop.otherFolder: Items from another folder tab left out: {{count}}. The context of a prompt is this folder's.

mention.label: Files, folders and more to add to the context
mention.failed: The folder could not be searched. You can still use the path you typed.
mention.outside: Only what is inside this folder can be offered.
mention.noMatch: Nothing in the folder matches what you typed.
mention.truncated: There is more here than the list shows — type more of the name to narrow it.
mention.useTyped: Use “{{path}}” as typed — it is checked when you send
mention.selectionHint: what is selected in the editor

slash.label: Commands and skills of this installation

slash.unavailable: The commands are not available right now. Anything you type still goes as the prompt.
slash.noMatch: No command or skill matches what you typed.
